units.source_text: 柏木把这只猫讨回家去，夜间叫它睡在身旁，天一亮就起来照管它，不惜辛苦，悉心抚养。

en.t: Kashiwagi asked to take the cat home, had it sleep beside him at night, and rose at daybreak to look after it, sparing no effort as he cared for it with all his heart.

units.source_text: 这猫性情虽然不亲近人，也终于被他养驯了，动辄跑过来牵他的衣裾，或者躺在他身边和他戏耍。

en.t: Although the cat was by nature not friendly to people, in the end he tamed it; it would often run over and tug at the hem of his robe, or lie beside him and play with him.
Kashiwagi came to love it sincerely.

units.source_text: 有一次他烦闷之极，将身横卧在窗前席上，沉思默想。

en.t: Once, when he was utterly weary and depressed, he lay stretched out on the mat before the window, lost in deep thought.

units.source_text: 这小猫便走过来，向他“咪咪”地叫，那叫声实甚可爱。

en.t: The little cat came over and mewed at him, and its voice was truly very endearing.

units.source_text: 柏木伸手抚摸它，说道：“这坏东西，来催我眠了。”

en.t: Kashiwagi reached out to stroke it and said, "You naughty thing, have you come to urge me to sleep?"
A smile then appeared on his face.
He composed a poem on the spot:
